citation: U.S. Department of Energy. EnergyPlus Engineering Reference and Input Output Reference. https://energyplus.net/documentation
description: EnergyPlus is a whole-building energy simulation program that engineers, architects and researchers use to model energy consumption for heating, cooling, ventilation, lighting and plug and process loads, and water use, in buildings. It solves thermal zone conditions and HVAC response simultaneously with a heat-balance method, uses sub-hourly time steps, models air movement between zones, advanced windows, daylighting and glare, component-based HVAC, and supports Functional Mockup Interface import and export for co-simulation. It is developed with funding from the U.S. Department of Energy's Building Technologies Office, which releases two major versions a year; version 26.1.0 was released on 31 March 2026 and 26.2.0 was at release-candidate stage in September 2026. Coverage is generic: any building anywhere, driven by an EPW weather file for the site. It is a console program that reads text input (IDF or epJSON) and writes text output, shipped for Windows, macOS and Linux with IDF-Editor and EP-Launch; source code is on GitHub. Licence: open source under a permissive BSD-style licence, free of charge. Caveat: the engine has no modelling interface of its own; most users build models through OpenStudio or commercial front ends, and results depend heavily on input assumptions. Simulation uses are building energy demand for capacity planning and HVAC sizing, retrofit and design optimisation, and climate adaptation studies with future weather files. Related records: OpenStudio (DOE's modelling platform for EnergyPlus), NREL ResStock and ComStock (building stock models run with EnergyPlus), and the Modelica Buildings Library, with which it is coupled in Spawn of EnergyPlus.
inputs: IDF or epJSON building description (geometry, constructions, schedules, internal loads, HVAC systems, controls)
name: EnergyPlus
notes: EnergyPlus is catalogued as a model (a numerical building energy model distributed as a program); OpenStudio and commercial GUIs that run it are platforms. The GitHub organisation moved from NREL to NatLabRockies after NREL became the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR); the README badges and git remote answer at the new address on 2026-09-26. GitHub web pages are blocked in this environment, so the repository was read through raw.githubusercontent.com and git ls-remote.
outputs: Sub-hourly to annual zone conditions and thermal comfort
